scenario: AITA for insisting that my son’s therapist tells me why my son wants to see him. | My son [17] was always a normal boy, with many friends, very active and didn’t seam to have any kind of problem. But one day we he told us he needed to go see a therapist. We were really surprised by that, we never thought he will ask us something like that. We ask him why but he didn’t want to tell us. We were worried so we send him to a therapist and now he goes once a week. In our eyes he is still the same kid that before. We tried to think about things that he may have. We thought maybe he is bulimic or anorexic ( as he is very thin ) but he isn’t that skinny and those things tend to affect women, not men. We thought of depression but that also doesn’t seem very likely. We decided that theorizing wouldn’t give us an answer so we ask his therapist and refused, saying that he couldn’t say what my son told him. I told him that we didn’t want the specifics but at least the reason why he goes to therapy. But he refused again. We try to insist many times but he didn’t give up. And the day after, our son come to us and tell us that he know that we insisted on knowing why he wants therapy ( we don’t know if the therapist told him or maybe he hear us talking about it in the house ) and insulted us. He didn’t talk to us for the rest of the day. Now, we know that insist to know wasn’t the best idea but we are his parents and we deserve to know. We really are assholes?

Research suggests that having a dedicated day for introspection and self-reflection can have a lasting impact on one's behavior and attitude towards mistakes. Here are a few possible ways that Yom Kippur might influence one's approach to mistakes throughout the year: 1. **Increased self-awareness**: By dedicating a day to introspection, individuals may become more attuned to their thoughts, feelings, and actions. This increased self-awareness can lead to a greater understanding of their mistakes and a more nuanced approach to personal growth. 2. **Renewed commitment to personal growth**: The intense focus on self-reflection and forgiveness on Yom Kippur can create a sense of urgency and motivation to make positive changes in one's life. This renewed commitment to personal growth can lead to a greater sense of accountability and a more serious approach to mistakes. 3. **Greater empathy and understanding**: The tradition of seeking forgiveness and making amends on Yom Kippur can foster a deeper understanding of the impact of one's actions on others. This empathy can translate to a more compassionate and considerate approach to relationships and decision-making throughout the year. 4. **Reduced procrastination and avoidance**: By confronting mistakes and taking responsibility for them on Yom Kippur, individuals may become more inclined to address issues and make amends in a timely manner throughout the year, rather than putting it off or avoiding it altogether. 5. **A sense of accountability**: The ritual of Yom Kippur can create a sense of accountability, not just to oneself, but also to one's community and tradition. This sense of accountability can encourage individuals to take their mistakes more seriously and strive to do better in the future. It's worth noting that the impact of Yom Kippur on one's approach to mistakes can vary from person to person. Some individuals may find that the experience has a lasting impact, while others may find that the effects are more fleeting. However, for many people, Yom Kippur serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of personal growth, forgiveness, and accountability.
